# ECON 0100 | Demo C

Demos are similar to Checkpoints, often taken directly from past semesters. Work through the problems and check your work against mine. Practice answering clearly and completely. You are encouraged to work in small groups. Find a study room, grab some classmates, and work together on a whiteboard.

## Flummoxed by the Floo Powder Fiasco

Floo Powder is a magical commodity used by witches and wizards to transport themselves through fireplaces to different locations. While it's often convenient, its use is associated with negative environmental effects, including air pollution and the depletion of magical resources used to produce the powder. The Ministry's Bureau of Economic Analysis has estimated the externality to be ~~10 galleons~~ {++15 coins per tin++} with the following supply and demand equations:

$$
P_b = 120 - 2 Q_d \qquad\textit{and}\qquad P_s = Q_s
$$

{++Retuned for review: the source's demand was $P_b = 100 - 2 Q_d$ with an externality of 10, which puts the market quantity at 33.3. Delete this line.++}

## Q3 | Designing the Policy (C3.1)

The Ministry of Magic has hired you to design a policy that corrects the market failure caused by the negative externality of Floo Powder use. Discuss the policy intervention you would recommend, how it would impact the market for Floo Powder and its users, and the government's welfare associated with the policy.

{++a\) Policy type: *tax, subsidy* Policy size: \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ per tin (C3.1)++}

{++b\) Quantity traded with your policy: \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ (C3.1)++}

{++c\) The 6-coin tax in Q2 left the quantity at \_\_\_\_\_, which is: *above, at, below* the socially efficient quantity (C3.1)++}

## Patronus Lessons

{++Every winter, dementors drift through Hogsmeade, and the surest defense against them is the Patronus Charm. Private tutors sell lessons in the charm. Each witch or wizard who learns it also protects their neighbors from dementors, an external benefit of 6 coins per lesson. Prices are in coins and quantity is in lessons. The demand (marginal private benefit) and supply (marginal cost) equations for lessons are the following:++}

$$
P_b = 40 - \frac{1}{2} Q_d \qquad\textit{and}\qquad P_s = 10 + \frac{1}{4} Q_s
$$

<!--
Editor. Demo C is the Floo Powder Fiasco (kept every year) plus a new Patronus Lessons market, laid out like Demo B and built to the same plan as Checkpoint C: five questions, one per skill, two markets. Front: Q1-Q3 (Floo Powder). Back: Q4-Q5 (Patronus Lessons).
Sources. The Floo Powder story is MiniExam_C_v8 Question 1 (ECON_0100/Checkpoints/C/MiniExam_C_v8.md), the same story as Homework C 23F/24F Q2/Q3 (Part_C/C_Practice_Bank/Homework_C_F24.md Q3). The story paragraph is verbatim except the externality (10 galleons cut, 15 coins per tin added). The Q3 lead sentence is the source's first task sentence, verbatim. The source's task paragraph ("Start by using a graph... the government's welfare associated with the policy") is replaced by the lettered questions.
Claude-drafted (all in {++ ++}): the retune line under the equations, every lettered question and question lead, and the whole Patronus Lessons story, its curves, and Q4-Q5. Coins replace galleons, as in Demo B; "per tin" is a new unit, since the source gives none.
Retuned numbers. The source's curves (P = 100 - 2Q, P = Q, externality 10) give a market quantity of 33.3. Retuned: D: P = 120 - 2Q, S: P = Q, external cost 15. Patronus: D (MPB): P = 40 - Q/2, S: P = 10 + Q/4, external benefit 6, so MSB = 46 - Q/2.
Answer key. Q1: a) MSC = 15 + Q; b) market Q 40 (P 40); c) efficient Q 35 (P 50); d) DWL is the triangle between MSC and D from 35 to 40, corners (35, 50), (40, 55), (40, 40), area 37.5 (not asked); e) MSC 55, MB 40, too much. Q2: a) 38; b) buyers 44; c) sellers 38; d) buyers 4 more, sellers 2 less; e) buyers. Q3: a) tax, 15; b) 35 (buyers 50, sellers 35, not asked); c) 38, above. Q4: a) 6; b) 40; c) 48; d) B; e) too few. Q5: a) 52; b) buyers 14; c) sellers 23; d) MC 23, MSB 20, above.
Skillsheet conflict. C2.2's second bullet says "In a market without externalities, explain why the added trades beyond the efficient quantity have marginal cost above marginal benefit." Q5 puts the subsidy in a positive-externality market, larger than the external benefit (9 against 6), so the trades beyond the efficient quantity are lessons 49-52, and the comparison is with MSB. Proposed rewording: "When a subsidy exceeds the external benefit, identify the trades beyond the efficient quantity and show their marginal cost is above marginal social benefit."
Flags. (1) Q3 c) circles above / at / below rather than "short of / beyond / at": the 6-coin tax moves quantity from 40 toward 35 but stops at 38, so "short of" could read either way. (2) Q2 has no blank axes on the Demo, to keep Q1-Q3 on the front; the guide still draws the tax graph. (3) Plass round-trip not run (no Plass checkout); the file uses only the vocabulary of Demo B and the style guide, plus {++ ++} and ~~ ~~ inline.
-->
